extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria for petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment and petitions to revive abandoned patent applications under 37 CFR (including requirements for evidence of nonreceipt, timeliness, required replies, fees, terminal disclaimers, and special-case handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of applicant reply to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's reply must reach the Office within the shortened statutory period for reply dating from the date stamped or printed on the Office letter or within the extended time period obtained under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fully responsive reply must be timely filed to avoid abandonment. In no case may an applicant reply outside the SIX (6) MONTH statutory period or obtain an extension for more than FIVE (5) MONTHS beyond the date for reply set forth in an Office action. (See MPEP §§ 710–710.06.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency (full responsiveness) of reply
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply filed within the period may still result in abandonment if it is not fully responsive to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission, use form paragraph 7.95 rather than the paragraph notifying of insufficiency. Examiner must set forth why there was a failure to take 'complete and proper action' when using insufficiency paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying claims from a patent does not constitute a reply (unless sole basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copying claims from a patent when not suggested by the USPTO does not constitute a reply to the last Office action and will not save the application from abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: this will not save the application only if the last Office action relied solely on the patent for the rejection of all the claims rejected in that action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment by withdrawal or failure to prosecute appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may become abandoned through withdrawal of, or failure to prosecute, an appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, or through dismissal of appeals to the CAFC or civil action where no amendment had been filed putting the application in condition for issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment also results from failure to perfect an appeal as required by the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. See MPEP §§ 1215.01–1216.01 for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE does not toll reply periods and may withdraw appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an RCE improperly (e.g., without appropriate fee or required submission) will not toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action and may be treated as a withdrawal of an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An improper RCE will not operate to toll the running of the time period for reply; it may also be treated as a withdrawal of an appeal by the applicant. See MPEP § 706.07(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings per 35 U.S.C. 120 (copendency timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A second application is copending with an earlier application only if filed before the patenting, abandonment of, or termination of proceedings on the earlier application. 'Before' means 'not later than.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In various situations (e.g., failure to pay issue fee, losing an interference), proceedings on the earlier application are terminated as of specified dates; understand which date applies for copendency purposes (see MPEP § 711.02(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration vs. petition to revive (distinction and route selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant disputes that an application is abandoned in fact (e.g., sufficiency of reply, controlling dates), they may request reconsideration of the examiner's holding (no fee) or petition for revival under 37 CFR 1.137 (fee-required) if there is no dispute that the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a) requesting withdrawal of the holding of abandonment does not require a fee. A petition under 37 CFR 1.137 requires the appropriate petition fee and meets the statutory revival process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.135 — abandonment for failure to reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant fails to reply within the time provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution to save the application pursuant to 1.135 must include such complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require; amendments after final rejection or not responsive to the last action will not operate to save the application. A bona fide substantially complete reply with inadvertent omission may permit a new time period under § 1.134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival under 37 CFR 1.137 — unavoidable delay ( §1.137(a) requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For revival based on unavoidable delay, the petition must include the required reply, the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(l), a showing to the Director that the entire delay was unavoidable, and any required terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable petition under (a) must include: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action (unless previously filed); (2) petition fee (1.17(l)); (3) satisfactory showing that the entire delay was unavoidable; (4) any terminal disclaimer and fee per § 1.321/1.20(d) if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival under 37 CFR 1.137 — unintentional delay ( §1.137(b) requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: For revival based on unintentional delay, the petition must include the required reply, the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m), a statement that the entire delay was unintentional, and any required terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is question whether the delay was unintentional. The statement of unintentionality must cover the entire delay from due date to filing of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply content required with a petition to revive (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by the reply required to the outstanding Office action (the reply sufficient to have avoided abandonment had it been timely filed), unless previously filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for an extension of time under 1.136 and its fee are not required to be included with the reply. The nature of the required reply varies by circumstance (see next entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply when abandonment was due to failure to pay issue or publication fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the abandonment was for failure to pay the issue fee (or any portion) or the publication fee, the required reply to revive must include payment of the issue fee or any outstanding balance, or the publication fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a continuing application without payment of the issue fee or outstanding balance is not an acceptable reply for revival in such cases. If issue fee increased after Notice of Allowance, the Office will mail notice requiring payment of the balance then in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed forms of reply for nonprovisional abandoned for failure to prosecute (non-final action)
rubrics_metrics.description: For abandonment due to failure to reply to a non-final action, the required reply may be either an argument or amendment under 37 CFR 1.111, or the filing of a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or a CPA under 1.53(d) for design applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of a petition under 1.137 is not a determination that any 1.111 reply is complete. A petition may be granted if the reply appears bona fide; examiner may later require correction via a one-month shortened statutory period under 1.135(c) (extensions under 1.136 permitted). Failure to correct re-abandons the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply for abandonment due to failure to reply to a final action
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final action must include either an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114, or cancellation of, or appeal from, the rejection of each claim so rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For revival in this situation the reply must be one of: (A) a Notice of Appeal and appeal fee; (B) an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 that cancels all the rejected claims or otherwise prima facie places the application in condition for allowance; (C) filing an RCE (with submission meeting 1.111 and requisite fee) for utility/plant apps filed on/after June 8, 1995; or (D) filing a continuing application under 1.53(b) (or CPA under 1.53(d) for design). If a notice of appeal is the reply, the Director sets the brief filing period in the decision granting the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted evidence to show nonreceipt of Office action (petition to withdraw holding of abandonment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment for nonreceipt must show that the Office action was not received at the correspondence address of record and provide documentary proof (practitioner docketing system records, master docket report, file jacket, incoming mail log, calendar, reminder system, or individual docket record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must describe the system used for recording Office action reception and establish reliability. If no master docket exists, provide alternative evidence. Evidence of nonreceipt of other Office communications generally will not warrant withdrawal. Office may deny if circumstances suggest loss after receipt or practitioner has history of not receiving actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted evidence to show timely mailing/filing (Express Mail, postcard receipt, certificate of mailing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment relying on timely mailing must use the proper procedures and evidence: Express Mail petitions per 37 CFR 1.10(c)-(e),(g) (and PALM entry), postcard receipts as prima facie evidence, or certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8(b) with a personal-knowledge statement or corroborating evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When shown to have been mailed by Express Mail, the paper must be entered in PALM with the Express Mail date. A postcard receipt should be entered into PALM using the postcard receipt date. A certificate of mailing requires personal knowledge (signed by mailer) or supporting evidence (mailing log). Duplicate copy of the correspondence should be submitted when relying on 1.8(b). Applicant may notify the Office of a previous mailing before abandonment and should check private PAIR first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 (two-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless provided otherwise, any petition under this part not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice from which relief is requested may be dismissed as untimely; the two-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere filing of a petition will not stay any period for reply. This rule applies to petitions to the Director under 1.181; see 1.181(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of untimely petitions to withdraw holding of abandonment (terminal disclaimer, dismissal)
rubrics_metrics.description: An untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment under 1.181(f) may be dismissed as untimely, or the Office may require a terminal disclaimer as a condition of granting an untimely petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant intentionally delayed filing the petition, the Office may dismiss it solely on that basis. For certain classes of applications and filing-date categories (see separate entries), differing terminal disclaimer and timing rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer and timing rules — design, pre‑June 8, 1995 utility, pre‑June 8, 1995 plant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For design applications, utility applications filed before June 8, 1995, and plant applications filed before June 8, 1995: if applicant never receives notice of abandonment, petitions not filed within twelve months from the filing/submission date for which further action could be expected will not be treated on the merits (absent extraordinary circumstances) unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer and fee; if applicant receives notice of abandonment, petitions not filed within two months of the mail date will similarly not be treated on the merits unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period to be disclaimed equals the terminal part of any patent term equivalent to the period between (A) the relevant start date (two months after mailing of notice or twelve months from filing/submission) and (B) the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw. Form PTO/SB/62 is the appropriate terminal disclaimer form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer rules — utility/plant apps filed June 8, 1995–May 28, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility and plant applications filed on/after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000: a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment in general, but OPLA consultation is necessary if the holding involves a period during appellate review, an interference, or a secrecy order suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OPLA when the abandonment period overlaps Board appellate review, interference proceedings (including suspensions), or secrecy-order suspensions, since patent term extension reductions may need to be effected under 37 CFR 1.701(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer and patent-term-adjustment rules — utility/plant apps filed on/after May 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility and plant applications filed on or after May 29, 2000: a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment because patent term adjustment is automatically reduced under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(4) or 1.704(a) for delays attributable to failure to file timely petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment is not filed within two months from the mailing date and applicant did not receive the notice, patent term adjustment is reduced by the period during which applicant 'failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds enumerated for revival under 37 CFR 1.137 (scope of relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 provides for revival of abandoned applications and lapsed patents for failures to: (A) timely reply to an Office requirement in a provisional application; (B) timely prosecute in a nonprovisional application; (C) timely pay the issue fee for a design application; (D) timely pay the issue fee for a utility or plant application; and (E) timely pay any outstanding balance of the issue fee (lapsed patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be brought under the appropriate subsection (unavoidable vs unintentional) and accompanied by the required reply and fees as described in the revival requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant standard for petitions to revive as to bona fides of reply (non-final action)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed reply is to a non-final Office action, the petition may be granted if the reply appears to be bona fide and substantially complete, but grant is not a final determination of the reply's completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after revival, the examiner finds the reply lacking, the examiner should send a letter giving a one-month shortened statutory period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) for correction (extensions under 1.136 allowed). Failure to correct within that time re-abandons the application.
